summary: This interactive educational website aims to spark curiosity and allow students to learn about space exploration through fun, hands-on experiences. By combining engaging browser games with captivating animated storytelling videos, the platform brings historic space missions and complex planetary science to life in an easy-to-understand way. As players take on the role of a mission operator, they explore two distinct planetary environments: the Moon—Earth’s airless, cratered natural satellite—and Mars, the rocky, rust-colored Red Planet. Through interactive gameplay and visual storytelling, students guide rovers to collect heavy rock samples while managing real-world constraints like weight capacity, battery limits, and communication range from the lander.   By blending dynamic animations with curiosity-driven gameplay, the website empowers students to visualize how robotic missions operate and discover the wonders of space while having fun.
details:
Cosmic Footprints is an interactive educational website developed to help students and casual space enthusiasts rediscover NASA's historic missions and explore the scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

The platform fulfils the challenge objectives by bringing these forgotten space artifacts back to life through an engaging, story-driven learning experience.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Space Explorer allows students to begin their journey from an interactive Solar System map, where they can select the Moon or Mars to explore. They can then visit different mission locations and discover historical spacecraft and equipment, including the Apollo Eagle Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP science stations, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix and InSight.

Each exploration section provides information about the mission, its equipment and scientific discoveries. Students can watch animated mini-documentaries with narration and synchronized captions. They can also participate in interactive games that simulate selected mission activities, followed by quizzes and knowledge checks to test their understanding.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes learning engaging: Students learn through exploration, animation, games and interactive activities rather than relying only on textbooks.
  • Improves scientific understanding: Students discover how spacecraft, rovers and scientific instruments work.
  • Encourages active learning: Students make choices, complete challenges and answer questions.
  • Develops digital skills: Students interact with a digital learning platform and practise problem-solving.
  • Makes space history accessible: Important missions and their discoveries are presented in a student-friendly format.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to inspire curiosity about space science, technology and engineering. It encourages students to appreciate NASA's achievements and understand the scientific value of missions whose spacecraft and equipment remain on the Moon and Mars. Ultimately, Space Explorer hopes to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and space explorers while making STEM education more interactive and meaningful.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software were used?

The project was developed as a web-based application using the following technologies:

  • HTML: To structure the website, interactive sections, maps, documentaries and games.
  • Hardware: A computer or laptop can be used to access the website. No specialised space-related hardware is required.

5. How is the project creative?

Space Explorer combines several learning approaches in one platform. Instead of presenting information through ordinary text and pictures, it allows students to experience space exploration through an interactive journey.

Its creative features include:

  • Mission-location exploration: Students discover historical spacecraft and equipment through interactive map markers.
  • Animated mini-documentaries with Interactive Mission Stories: Space missions are explained through animated scenes, spoken narration and synchronised captions.
  • Mission-based games: Students experience simplified activities inspired by real missions, such as operating the Lunar Roving Vehicle, deploying ALSEP equipment and controlling robotic explorers.
  • Interactive quizzes: Students can check their understanding after exploring each mission.

6. What factors did the team consider?

When developing Space Explorer, the team considered several important factors:

  1. Historical and scientific accuracy: Mission information and scientific discoveries needed to be presented responsibly and clearly.
  2. Student engagement: Activities needed to be interesting enough to encourage students to explore independently.
  3. Educational value: Every documentary, game and quiz should support learning about space missions and technology.
  4. Ease of use: Navigation and instructions should be simple and suitable for students.
  5. Accessibility: The website should be usable through common web browsers and different screen sizes.
  6. Creativity and innovation: The team wanted to combine interactive maps, animated storytelling and games into one learning platform.
  7. Responsible representation: Animated scenes are presented as educational illustrations rather than original NASA archival footage.

Conclusion

Space Explorer is more than an educational website. It is an interactive learning experience that brings forgotten space missions back into students' attention. By combining technology, creativity and scientific knowledge, the project transforms historical space exploration into an exciting adventure. It encourages students to explore, question, discover and appreciate the achievements of space science while inspiring them to become future innovators and explorers.
